Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:1: After having spoken, in the previous chapters, of the matter of the holiness of all the organs of the head, we come to explain the matter of the holiness of the covenant [brit], concerning conjugal union, how its holiness shall be. And we shall explain in this two aspects: the first, the existence of the holiness of union itself; the second, the timing of union. And we shall not trouble ourselves to copy the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, which the sage Rabbi Yitzchak Aboab has already copied in his Sefer Menorat HaMaor, and we shall rely on the reader to see his words there, for they are necessary for the practical knowledge of many details; however, in this chapter we shall copy only the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him, scattered here and there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:2: Our holy Torah commanded us (Leviticus 11:44), "and you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy" - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained that this holiness is said concerning the holiness of conjugal relations - these are their words, in the chapter "Yedi'ot HaTum'ah" (Shevuot 18b): Rabbi Binyamin ben Yefet said, whoever sanctifies himself at the time of conjugal relations shall have male children, as it is written, "and you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy," and juxtaposed to it, "a woman who conceives" - to this point. And likewise, the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in Parashat Tazria (page 49a) agree with this, as we shall copy below concerning the timing of union.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:3: And so they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Kedoshim, page 81a) that this is also what is said in "you shall be holy" (Leviticus 19:2) - these are its words: come and see, at the time a person is found in one union, male and female, and intends to sanctify properly, then he is complete and called "one" without blemish - therefore a person must gladden his wife at that time, to invite her with one desire together with him, and both of them shall intend as one for that matter; and when the two of them are found as one, then all is one in soul and in body - in soul, to cleave one to the other with one desire, and in body, as we have learned, that an unmarried person is like one who is divided; and when male and female join together, they become one body - it follows that they are one soul and one body, and called one person. Then the Holy One, blessed be He, rests upon "one," and brings forth a spirit of holiness within that "one," and these are called children of the Holy One, blessed be He, as stated - and therefore "you shall be holy, for I, the LORD, am holy." Happy are Israel, who established this matter only in Him truly, as it is written, "for I, the LORD, am holy," in order to cleave to Him and not to another - and therefore, "you shall be holy, for I, the LORD your God, am holy" - to this point. Behold, from the end of the teaching it is explicit that the mitzvah "you shall be holy" concerns the holiness of union - and what it explained concerning the matter of the holiness of union we shall further explain below.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:4: And know that according to how a person sanctifies himself at that hour, so shall he draw a holy soul to his child - and so it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Shemot, page 11b) - these are its words: "and a man of the house of Levi went" (Exodus 2:1) - this is Gabriel, as it is said (Daniel 9:21), "and the man Gabriel whom I had seen in the vision," and so on; "of the house of Levi" - this is Knesset Yisrael, which comes from the side of the left. "And he took a daughter of Levi" - this is the soul, for we have learned that at the time the body of a righteous person is born in this world, the Holy One, blessed be He, calls Gabriel and takes that soul of the righteous one that is in the Garden, and brings it down to this body of the righteous one born in this world, and he is appointed over it and guards it. And if you say, that angel appointed over the spirits of the righteous is named Laylah [Night], and you say it is Gabriel - so it is indeed, because it comes from the side of the left, and everything coming from the side of the left is called thus. "And the man went" - this is Amram; "and he took a daughter of Levi" - this is Yocheved; and a heavenly voice went down and told him to marry her, for the time of Israel's redemption was drawing near, through the son to be born from them, and the Holy One, blessed be He, assisted him - for we have learned, the Shechinah rested upon their bed, and their desire was in one cleaving with the Shechinah - and therefore the Shechinah did not depart from that son they bore, to endure - as it is written, "and you shall sanctify yourselves and be holy": a person sanctifies himself from below, the Holy One, blessed be He, sanctifies him from above; just as their desire was in cleaving to the Shechinah, so the Shechinah cleaved to that very act they performed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:5: Rabbi Yitzchak said: happy are those righteous whose desire is in cleaving to the Holy One, blessed be He, continually - and just as they cleave to Him continually, so too He cleaves to them and never abandons them. Woe to the wicked whose desire and cleaving are distanced from Him, and it does not suffice them to be distanced from Him, but they cleave to the other side. Come and see: Amram, who cleaved to the Holy One, blessed be He, from him came forth Moses - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:6: Further, in the Zohar (Parashat Chayei Sarah, end of page 130) - these are its words: in this manner, every person of the world is composed of above and below, and all those who know to sanctify themselves in this world properly, when they beget a child, a spirit of holiness rests upon him from the place from which all holy things emerge, and these are called children of the Holy One, blessed be He - because the body was made in holiness properly, so too they are given a spirit from the supernal holy place, as is fitting, and this has already been stated - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:7: And know that the existence of the holiness of union depends on a person's knowledge of how to cleave to the Holy One, blessed be He, and to know how to unite the attributes in spiritual existence - for just as he knows how to divest the physicality of things above, so he must know how to divest his thought from thinking of that act as an entry into the vanity of the pleasure of this world - for one who directs this act toward pleasure resembles a beast, as we have written in this Gate, chapter 4, concerning one who sanctifies himself even below, and as we elaborated in the Gate of Love, chapter 10, in explaining the teaching of Rashbi, peace be upon him. And therefore it said in this teaching before us, "happy are those righteous whose desire is in cleaving to the Holy One, blessed be He, continually" - for the righteous, whose intent is always to cleave to Him, are not separated from Him even at that time - and this is what it means by "continually."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:8: And the parallel to this is the matter of the intent of eating that we wrote above in the previous chapters - that although the bodily organs enjoy that eating, the thought clings above, to think of the spirituality of the eating; likewise in this matter is the existence of union.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:9: And what the reader needs to know, how to divest himself entirely, in union, from the aspect of the evil inclination, is that he should think that the aspect of that organ is an organ like the rest of the 248 organs of a person, some revealed, some hidden - and behold, before the sin of Adam it is said (Genesis 2:25), "and the two of them were naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed" - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in Vayikra Rabbah, at the beginning of Parashat Acharei Mot: Rabbi Levi in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya, the heel of Adam would dim the orb of the sun, how much more so the countenance of his face - see there. And so it says in the Tikkunim (page 10b), at first "garments of light," by which his heel would dim the orb of the sun, and so on - and certainly his other organs too were, in this proportion, more luminous, and the evil inclination did not rule over them, and therefore "they were not ashamed." And what caused them shame? From the side of the nakedness [ervah], which is the evil inclination that blemished them; but before this, that organ was to them like a hand or a foot - since the mitzvah of the union of a man and his wife is through this organ, it is like the placing of tefillin on the left hand and the tefillin of the head on the brain - and just as these have no evil inclination in them, so too in that organ, which fulfills the mitzvah of being fruitful and multiplying that Adam was commanded before the sin, all is one, and it is not fitting that there be an evil inclination in it. And what caused there to be an evil inclination in it, and that it need covering, and that it be called ERVAH [nakedness]? The sin that was in it was the blemish that is RA [evil] and VAH [in it], and it drew after itself its foreskin, and became physical, and the evil inclination ruled over this organ.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:10: And the essential task of the righteous in this world is to repair the blemish of Adam, for Adam included all souls, all of which sinned, and all of which need to be repaired. Now, the righteous who cleave to the Holy One, blessed be He, in the secret of their thought repair the secret of the supernal thought in which Adam's blemish occurred, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 99b), that Adam sinned in thought and Eve in deed - see there, and further see page 113 - and through the repair of thought, which is Yud, the lower Yud that is in the covenant is necessarily repaired.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:11: And the reason for this is that when a person's thought is on worldly matters of licentiousness, and his heart is after matters of coarse matter, then the Yud of the covenant is blemished, for immediately his bow becomes drawn, as it is written (Leviticus 19:4), "do not turn to the idols and become impure through them" - as explained in Parashat Kedoshim (page 84a), that one who gazes at a woman and thinks of her by day is made impure by her at night, and his impurity is through the sign of the covenant, which is the Yud, which includes within it all the organs of the body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:12: And this was the sin of Adam's blemish, that he gave dominion over his whole body to the evil inclination, and uprooted himself from the supernal spirituality of holiness, divested of the evil inclination, and clothed himself in the coarse matter of the world and its powers, and in licentiousness and the like from the other husks - for the husk of licentiousness is the one that includes everything. And therefore our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said that the Holy One, blessed be He, is jealous of licentiousness more than all other transgressions, and the reason is that a person uproots himself and his organs and his soul from all holiness and clothes himself entirely in the evil inclination, unlike the other transgressions - except for the matter of eating, which is also an inclusive transgression that defiles the soul, because that impurity becomes a portion, an organ, in his body - and licentiousness is equal to it, for the term "eating" is also said of it, as it is said (Proverbs 30:20), "she eats and wipes her mouth."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:13: And when a person cleaves continually to the Holy One, blessed be He, and does not think of matters of transient, corruptible matter, and desires only to cleave to the root essence of life that gives life to all, which is the secret of love explained in the Gate of Love - certainly then his bow does not become drawn, and he shall not come to impurity in any way, and then his union shall be holy and shall not be drawn at all toward the side of the evil inclination, but rather his matter shall be as Adam was before his sin, that it be solely for the fulfillment of a mitzvah - for in the mitzvah he resembles his Maker, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the teaching we copied from Parashat Kedoshim, that just as He, blessed be He, is holy, so He commanded us to be holy, as it says at the end of the teaching, happy are Israel, who established this matter only in Him truly, as it is written, "for I, the LORD," and so on - meaning that just as the existence of union, namely "I, the LORD," is called holy, being divested of the evil inclination, so we must resemble Him, because the essence of holiness pertains to our souls, the spiritual ones emanated from Him, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:14: And if, God forbid, one thinks in this act of vain pleasure, it follows that he clothes his spiritual soul in the evil inclination, the opposite of the divine intent - and for this King David, peace be upon him, warned us (Psalms 32:9), "be not like a horse or mule without understanding," and so on - and it is explained there in Parashat Kedoshim (page 80a), at the beginning of the explanation of this verse, concerning the matter of union - these are its words: happy are the righteous who occupy themselves with Torah and know the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, and sanctify themselves with the holiness of the King, and are found holy in everything - and therefore they draw a spirit of holiness from above, and all their children are truly righteous and are called children of the King, holy children. Woe to the wicked, who are all brazen and whose deeds are brazen - therefore their children inherit a brazen soul from the impure side, and as it is written (Leviticus 11:43), "and you shall become impure through them" - he comes to be impure, they make him impure. "Be not like a horse or mule" - who are the masters of licentiousness over all. "Without understanding" - that people not occupy themselves in this way, for if so, it is written here "without understanding," and it is written there (Isaiah 56:11), "and the dogs are greedy of soul, they know no satiety, and they are shepherds who know no understanding" - meaning, behold, those called "greedy of soul" are found, because they know no understanding. "And they are shepherds" - what is "shepherds"? These are those who lead and guide a person to Gehinnom. "They know no satiety" - as it is said (Proverbs 30:15), "the leech has two daughters, give, give" - therefore, those who are "give, give" know no satiety. "They all turn to their own way, each to his own gain from his own quarter" - for they are the residents of Gehinnom, and who caused all this? Because they did not sanctify themselves in that union as needed - and therefore it is written (Leviticus 19:2), "you shall be holy, for I am holy" - the Holy One, blessed be He, said, of all the other nations My desire was not to cleave to it except to Israel, as it is written (Deuteronomy 4:4), "but you who cleave to the LORD" - you, and not the other nations who worship idols - and therefore it is written here, "holy" - therefore "you shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy" - "you shall be holy" precisely - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:15: Behold, concerning the punishment of one who does not sanctify himself - and the essence of holiness depends on a person being occupied with Torah and cleaving to it properly, so that he not come to think of licentiousness - and this is what it said at the beginning of the teaching, happy are those who occupy themselves with Torah. And it is further explained there, before this, concerning the punishment of the common people who are not occupied with Torah, that they draw for their children a soul that is not holy - for Torah guides a person and teaches him how to sanctify himself.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:16: And what it said at the end of the teaching, "you shall be holy," precisely - it seems to me that the intent is to be precise about the word "tihyu" [you shall be], that the intent is the language of existence [havayah], to allude to the coming-into-being of the souls, that they be in holiness - for otherwise it would say "and you shall sanctify yourselves," as it said earlier in the chapter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:17: And if you say, if a person sanctifies his thought and removes it from thinking of physicality, he shall never come to arousal - and how is it possible that there be union of the soul now, in our time, and that it be in holiness - for these two things contradict one another? One can say that we have learned the way of a person's sanctification from Rashbi, peace be upon him, in several places - one, in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Tzav, beginning of page 34) - these are its words: and the offering of the letters - they are Yud in "ish" [man], Hei in "ishah" [woman], Vav in the son, the bridegroom, Hei in the bride. Happy is he who brings near the letters of YHVH within himself, his wife, his son, and his daughter, in holiness, in blessing, in cleanliness, in humility, in bashfulness, and in all the good attributes written concerning the masters of the Mishnah - and they warm themselves with holy fires, of fire [esh] and woman [ishah], which are a fire ascending and descending: the holiness of the wood of the arrangement, which are the holy pieces of wood, holy organs, and the fire from Above descends, which is the Holy of Holies - and concerning these two fires the prophet said (Isaiah 24:15), "therefore in the lights, honor the LORD" - for they are the fires of the great Shechinah, "for the LORD your God is a consuming fire" (Deuteronomy 4:24) - and they are: the supernal fire, the throne of mercy; the lower fire, the throne of judgment - and this is Binah and Malchut - Malchut, an ascending fire; Binah, a descending fire; YHVH, the middle pillar, holds both of them. Binah is YHVH, Malchut, Tiferet - when it holds them, Chochmah rests upon it, within which is the "power [koach] of MaH," which is Yud-Kei-Vav-Kei, its power being Yud-Vav-Dalet Hei-Aleph Vav-Aleph-Vav Hei-Aleph, and all these forty-two letters are found in a person, his wife, and his children - and therefore no person is complete except with a son and a daughter; and one who has no son, who is Vav, the Yud is removed; and one who has no daughter has no Hei, which is the daughter - the supernal Hei is removed, which is the mother of his mate, for the letters do not rest, one without the other. And therefore, in the man and the woman, son and daughter, when done properly, YHVH rests upon them and they are called children to the Holy One, blessed be He - this is what is written (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children to the LORD your God" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:18: And what is relevant to our discourse is the matter of what it said, "and they warm themselves with holy fires of man and woman" - as explained in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer, that between man and woman the Name Yud-Hei is placed, and when man and woman conduct themselves properly, the Shechinah is between them, and if not, God forbid, the Name Yud-Hei departs and only fire and fire remain, and fire "consumes until destruction" (Job 31:12). Now, the fire that is in the man is sweetened more than the judgment of the woman, for in the man the Yud is placed between the Aleph and the Shin, but in the woman the Hei is at its end - and its secret is: ISH [man] is a descending fire, ISHAH [woman] is an ascending fire - and it is known that every descent is the flow descending in descent, for everything descending swiftly goes the straight way to bestow, while the female is a returning light, and is called ISHAH, an ascending fire, meaning it ascends in order to receive. And one must intend that his organs are warmed through the higher fire, which is the Holy of Holies bestowed from Binah, which is the Holy of Holies, and likewise he is warmed through the ascending fire from the Shechinah, and this is from the fire that is in his wife - as it said in the teaching, "YHVH, the middle pillar, holds both of them," and saying "holds," it appears that he grasps from both these fires mentioned - namely as it says, "therefore in the lights, honor the LORD" - so he is warmed by a holy fire for the sake of a mitzvah, the holiness of union. And there is a further secret of fire: it is the secret of the Name Elohim, which equals ESH [fire] in its full spelling, and the throne [HaKisei] equals Elohim.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:19: And my teacher, peace be upon him, explained concerning "they warm themselves with holy fires," that it is to guard against being warmed by a strange, foreign fire - as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Acharei Mot, page 77a) - these are its words: and sometimes it happens that Na'amah goes forth to the world to warm herself with people, and a person is found bound in desire with her, and he awakens from his sleep and holds his wife and lies with her, his desire being in that longing that he had in his dream - then that person who begets [a child] comes from the side of Na'amah, for it was in his desire that this happened, for when Lilith went forth and saw him and knew the matter, she becomes bound to him, and so on - it says there that that person is harmed every month. Happy are the righteous who sanctify themselves with the holiness of the King - of them it is written (Isaiah 66:23), "and it shall be, from new moon to new moon" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:20: And one must intend that the evil inclination aroused for union is from the side of Gevurah, which is a holy fire, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Bereishit, beginning of page 49), on the verse (Genesis 2:7), "and the LORD God formed [vayitzer] man" - these are its words: but "and the LORD God formed [vayitzer]" - included with two Yuds, the good inclination and the evil inclination; why? Rather, the good inclination is for himself, the evil inclination is to arouse toward the female, and from the side of the left it always arouses toward the female. The secret of the matter: from here we learn that the north always arouses toward the female and binds with her, and therefore she is called ISHAH [woman, from ESH, fire]. And come and see, the good inclination and the evil inclination - because the female was given between them and bound with them, but she is not bound until the evil inclination arouses toward her, and they bind one with the other; and once they bind one with the other, then the good inclination, which is joy, is aroused and brings her toward him - and above, the side of the north itself, which is joy without the defilement of the evil inclination, grasps her first, as it is written (Song of Songs 2:6), "his left hand is under my head," and afterward, "and his right hand embraces me" - and then she is given between them to be repaired. And therefore "and the LORD God formed" - there, the full Name, toward these two sides, the good inclination and the evil inclination; "man" - we have already established, but male is not separated from female to be face to face - to this point. Behold, it is explained that above, Gevurah, which is the left, from which the evil inclination is drawn, is what arouses union - and the explanation of our intent is what was explained above, that in Atzilut there is no evil inclination, God forbid, and this is what it said, "without the defilement of the evil inclination" - for in the continuation of judgment downward, into the externals, the evil inclination becomes defiled, meaning that its inclination desires pleasure and the like; but above it is joy alone, aroused from the left, and it is the spiritual fire in the secret of the Name Elohim, as it said that the good inclination and the evil inclination were created in the full Name YHVH Elohim - meaning YHVH, the good inclination, to guide the male, which are the acts of kindness, and the evil inclination, Elohim, which are the acts of severity, to guide the female, who is ISHAH, the fire of Hei - and this is "man" [ha'adam], which is the union of male and female face to face, the union of Chesed and Din, YHVH Elohim. Behold, when a person thinks in the aspect of the inclination to arouse it for the sake of holiness, the inclination itself becomes sanctified and resembles its supernal root.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:21: And it appears to me that if arousal comes upon a person that he did not intend for the sake of a mitzvah, he should dig his fingernails into the ground, and likewise reflect on the day of death, until his desire is nullified - and afterward, at the time of union, he should return and arouse himself for the sake of holiness, along the lines stated, by thinking of the holy Names mentioned - and in this way he guards the drop from the evil inclination, as explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 17, page 27) - these are its words: and in the same way, in a person's union, he must purify the drop from sin, which is the evil inclination, so that the seed be clean in Hei - this is what is written (Genesis 47:23), "behold, seed for you" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:22: And nevertheless, since it is impossible for a person to be entirely clean of the evil inclination, because he is clothed in the matter of the [physical] inclination after Adam's sin, and matter necessarily has pleasure even though he intends whatever he wishes - for this reason a person becomes impure through the emission of the drop, since the evil inclination has clothed itself in him in any case.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:23: And concerning the holiness of union and its intent, they explained in the Tikkunim (page 25a) that it resembles the unification a person performs in the Amidah prayer, and it said there that just as when a person prays the Amidah it is silently, so union must be silent - these are its words: at the time they are in one union, Israel must stand in prayer silently, and the secret of the matter, they bring her in silently, and therefore, when Israel stand in the Amidah to arouse toward her the eighteen blessings silently, to pour blessings upon her - it is said of the Chayot (Ezekiel 1:24), "when they stood, they let down their wings," that there is no need to make a sound heard - along the lines of Chanah, of whom it is said (I Samuel 1:13), "and her voice was not heard." And so Israel must unite with their mate silently, in humility, in trembling and fear, covered - as the early ones established, like one overcome by a demon, which is a demon from Shaddai [i.e. from the very name of God, playing on the word], for at that time it passes through the doorway - and this is the secret of the mezuzah, of which it is said (Deuteronomy 6:9), "and you shall write them on the doorposts [mezuzot] of your house" - "mezuzot" is written [alluding to] MEZIMOT [plots/schemes]; and if his voice is heard, immediately "sin crouches at the door" (Genesis 4:7) - and moreover, he is thereby small in faith, and it is not for nothing that the early ones established, anyone who makes his voice heard in his prayer is among those of little faith - to this point, concerning the matter of union.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:24: Further, there: at the time they unite, "let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth" - what is "the kisses of his mouth"? Two lips of his and two of hers, which are the four wings of the Chayot, of which it is said (Ezekiel 1:6), "and each had four wings" - and when his two faces and her two faces are joined, and the four arms of the two of them, of which it is said (Ezekiel, ibid.), "and each had four faces and each of them four wings" - and these are the four faces, YHVH; the four wings, Adonai; in one joining, YAHDONHY [the unified Names] - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:25: And what it said, to unite with his mate in trembling, fear, and covering - so it also appears in the Zohar (Parashat Va'etchanan, page 269a) - these are its words: "and when you lie down" - to conduct oneself in fear of one's Master, in holiness, in humility, that he not be found brazen before his Master - to this point. And certainly one who has relations without covering is brazenness - and so they said in the Gemara (Niddah 16b, see Tosafot s.v. "u'mashtin"), three the Holy One, blessed be He, hates, and one of them is one who has relations naked. Nevertheless, this does not come to exclude that he have relations in his garment, for they said (Ketubot 48a), "he in his garment and she in her garment" - he shall divorce and give her the ketubah [if he refuses otherwise].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:26: And Rashbi explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 58, page 92a) - these are its words: and at that time when she divests herself of these garments, she unites with her husband in closeness of flesh - this is what is written (Genesis 2:23), "bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called Woman, for from Man she was taken. Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and cleave to his wife, and they shall become one flesh" - for this is the way male and female unite, in closeness of flesh, and this is the joining of the union above, that nothing intervene - and therefore the masters of the Mishnah established that a person praying and uniting the Holy One, blessed be He, with His Shechinah must have nothing intervening between him and the wall, without separation or division between the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah - and the secret of the matter (ibid. 2:25), "and the two of them were naked, the man and his wife" - naked, in closeness of flesh without any garment at all - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:27: And let us return to the teaching from Parashat Kedoshim that we copied above, and explain in it something according to the plain sense, for in this teaching the intent of union is explained, what it shall be. It said, therefore a person must gladden his wife at that time - one of the good intents that the Ra'avad, peace be upon him, wrote in the Gate of Holiness, as Rabbeinu Yaakov, Ba'al HaTurim, copied in Tur Orach Chaim (siman 240), is that he intend the mitzvah of fulfilling conjugal duty [onah], which is a positive commandment (Exodus 21:10), "her conjugal rights he shall not diminish" - and this is what it said, "a person must gladden his wife," to invite her with one desire together with him - meaning that her desire should be bound with him, that there be no accusation or dispute between them, but rather love, brotherhood, peace, and companionship - and especially on the Sabbath. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (page 57a), that he must say to her words of appeasement - and so it is explained in Parashat Bereishit (Zohar, Parashat Bereishit, page 49b) - these are its words: from here we learn, one who unites with his wife must please her and sweeten her with words, and if not, he should not lodge with her, in order that their desire be as one, without coercion, and so on - and it explains there words of love: "this time, bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called Woman" - see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:28: "And both of them shall intend as one for that matter" - meaning that he must tell her to direct her mind toward holiness, to draw a holy soul together with the union, to beget in soul and in body, so that they resemble the supernal existence - for just as, through this, Ze'ir Anpin and his mate cleave together in their inwardness and outwardness as one, so below they must resemble their root, and this is what it means by "one soul and one body." And it appears from the language that one must intend that just as the body of man is completed from his lack - namely the rib that was taken from man when he unites - so his soul, too, is lacking, since souls, too, when emanated from above, are emanated male and female, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Lech Lecha, page 91b) concerning the matter of "the daughter of so-and-so to so-and-so" - and below they are separated; it follows that in union the souls are completed, male in female, and likewise in the existence of their bodies, as explained - and this is "one soul and one body," that just as there is unity in the body, so in the soul. And this premise is necessary and true without any doubt, and there is no room here to elaborate.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:29: "Then the Holy One, blessed be He, rests upon 'one' and brings forth a spirit of holiness" - the matter is that just as in the supernal existence we have that the Infinite, blessed and exalted be He, does not rest His unity upon a blemished Throne, but only when it is entirely united as one do they then shine with supernal light - so in the lower existence, when they unite with the intent stated, they merit that they have a holy soul, and this is what it means by "a spirit of holiness."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:30: "Happy are those who established this matter only in Him truly" - meaning the secret of the supernal Atzilut, namely "I am the LORD," and not in the lower worlds. And it said, "and therefore, 'you shall be holy, for I, the LORD your God, am holy'" - these are the secret of nefesh, ru'ach, neshamah that come into being from the side of the supernal union, and this suffices for the one who understands.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:31: And so it is fitting to intend what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, Parashat Bereishit, page 12b), the sixth commandment, to occupy oneself with being fruitful and multiplying - and whoever occupies himself with being fruitful and multiplying causes that river to flow continually, and its waters do not cease, and the sea is completed from all sides, and new souls are renewed and go forth from that tree, and many hosts increase above together with those souls - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:32: And it is included in the holiness of union that the union be face to face and not face against back, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Pekudei, page 259a) - these are its words: here is the union and the binding as one, that above and below be one in binding, that no organ be separated from another, and that all be found face to face - and therefore we have learned, whoever has relations with his bed [i.e. his wife] from behind weakens the arrangement of gazing face to face, to illuminate everything as one, and to be found face to face in cleaving properly, as it is said (Genesis 2:24), "and he shall cleave to his wife" - "to his wife" precisely, and not "after his wife" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:33: And the matter of "after his wife" is the overturning of the table, which they spoke of in Tractate Nedarim (page 20a): why are the lame born? Because they overturn their table - and Rashi, peace be upon him, explained: that they turn face toward the back, coming upon their wives not in their natural manner. And so Rabbeinu Asher wrote: because they overturn their table, having relations not in the natural manner - measure for measure, since he burdens her upon her knees, therefore his children are lame-footed - to this point. And everything found afterward in the Gemara about the overturning of the table that they permitted in the Gemara, where it said (ibid. 20b), a certain woman came before Rav and said to him, I set the table for him and he overturned it, and he said, how does this differ from a cake? - this is certainly its explanation. And I have written this to exclude those who cast off from themselves fear and shame and emit their seed in vain, having relations in the impure orifice, the place of excretion - for relations there cannot beget, and indeed they said, why are the lame born? Because they overturn their table. And Rambam, peace be upon him, wrote in chapter 21 of the Laws of Forbidden Relations, that he should not emit seed in vain (halachah 9) - and if relations there are indeed in vain [of no procreative purpose], and so it appears from the words of the Ra'avad, peace be upon him, in the Gate of Holiness, that the intent concerning the overturning of the table mentioned is only face against back, and its matter concerns procreation, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:34: And I found that my teacher, peace be upon him, wrote of ways for a person to sanctify himself, and among them explained something of the holiness of conjugal relations, and we shall copy his words here - these are its words: the way a person rides upon the external [forces], and how many aspects there are to it, requiring cunning to be saved from it - the essential thing on which everything depends is the foundation of every single matter: it must have no grasp at all, along the lines of what is said (Jeremiah 22:13), "woe to him who builds his house without righteousness [tzedek]" - and Tzedek is Malchut; and this is one whose every deed is for the sake of Heaven, the secret of unification: "shem" [name] is Malchut, "shamayim" [heaven] is Tiferet - and when a person places "the sake of Heaven" foremost in all his deeds, the husk immediately departs from there; but if his deeds are not for the sake of Heaven, evil immediately leaps there and rules over that matter. Therefore a person's deeds must be for the sake of Heaven: in thought, that he direct his thought in that act for the sake of the union of his Maker, as is known; in speech, that he mention with his mouth, for the sake of the union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah; and in deed, that the deed not be corrupted - for thought and speech shall not avail if the vessel is unseemly, it shall not rest. And for this, when he is "building a house," his thought shall be for the service of his Maker, and his speech for the sake of Heaven - the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah - and his deed [likewise], and then righteousness shall lodge in that matter, and evil shall be separated from there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:35: And this is a great principle in procreation, in the union of a man and his wife, for there is nothing that hastens the wicked Lilith to be found there more than this act - because it is a great building, either to beget an enduring child, one who builds the world, or to beget children in haste for the sake of Lilith, as explained in the Sabba (Parashat Mishpatim, page 96a-b) concerning the oppressed, or to beget wicked ones, children of Samael and Lilith, destroyers of the world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:36: And therefore this matter is extremely difficult, and requires great matters and preparations to flee from her - and the first preparation is a person's purification from his sins, as much as possible, through repentance before his Maker. The second preparation is to guard oneself from sin while she is a niddah [menstruant], for then she is shared with his wife [i.e. the impure force has a hold], and if he sins with her thereafter, it attaches to him afterward in her offspring. The third preparation is the woman's purification properly and fittingly, as is known, and the cutting of her fingernails - the twenty that grew during her niddah - which cause harm to the world, and likewise some of her hair, as explained at the end of Parashat Acharei Mot (page 79a), and likewise in the Zohar (Parashat Pinchas, end, page 248), that she should store them in her courtyard in a known corner, and when she immerses, burn them, since that portion belongs to the impure side, its portion of impurity, and it needs elimination, and there is no elimination except by burning. The fourth preparation is his union with her in holiness, with intent of heart, and with modesty - and in the Zohar, Parashat Vayikra (page 19a), it explains a certain incantation to be said at the time of union, in order to distance this wickedness from him; and it has already been explained in the Bar Mitzva [i.e., in a similar work] the sign of the holy way, that he sanctify himself at the time of relations, and the essential thing overall is that it not be by candlelight and that it be covered - and likewise that he wash his hands after midnight, before union, in order to remove the spirit of impurity.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:37: And along this way a person shall distance himself from all things that cause a blemish to the soul, for she [the impure force] has entry through all of them, and he shall distance himself from all filthy things and from all places where the harmful ones are found, for all of these shall cause him harm - and likewise from houses of idolatry, such as their houses of worship, their courts, their places of assembly, to distance himself four cubits from a harlot, and not to gaze in his thought at their licentiousness and the like - for these things cause harm to a person, and immediately the harlot woman pursues him, to lead him into forbidden licentiousness even within what is permitted to him, and the like of evil things - besides several other matters, such as all kinds of sorceries and divinations, and gazing at them, for a person is subject to chance with them, since they are ready for a person in an instant, and this is their joy, to cling to him. And above all, he should beware of being one of strife and quarrel within his house, for this is her essential preparation, for she is immediately found there. And when he knows that he is opposite the supernal Bridegroom and she opposite the supernal Bride, and by making a quarrel he drives away peace from between the two, and immediately wickedness takes hold there - there is no doubt that a person shall see that this is a great blemish. And quarreling in the house of a woman giving birth causes danger to the child, and it is immediately found there. And quarreling in a place of joy, such as [the house of] a bridegroom and bride, God forbid, causes great harm and takes hold in that house, along the lines of (Jeremiah 22:13), "woe to him who builds his house without righteousness."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:38: And so he should beware of the repugnant things she holds onto, and of eating them in filthy places, for it was not for nothing that they explained (Makkot 16b), "you shall not make your souls detestable" (Leviticus 11:43) - this refers to one who drinks from the cupping-horn of the bloodletter - for all these things cause the soul's detestation with this wickedness, whose dwelling is in filth. And likewise he should beware of not being soiled in his hands and filthy in his garments - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, have already warned Torah scholars of this, and explained the reason (Shabbat 114a), "all who hate Me love death" (Proverbs 8:36) - certainly death, which is she, without doubt. And he should not eat casually, by chance, unless with intent, sitting for the honor of his Maker, for she too happens by chance. And he should not bless with soiled and filthy hands, and the like - and our Sages, of blessed memory, have already elaborated on this - all these are prohibitive commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:39: And there are positive commandments, such as being careful with Havdalah after blessing, to pray until they [the forces of impurity] separate from him, for then they grow stronger, and one must elaborate in verses of protection according to his ability. And likewise upon leaving the doorway of his house, and all the more so at night, and [invoking] the protection of his Maker at the doorway, and as he goes out and separates from her [his house/the impure force], the external force being to his left, he should pray there to his Maker that His protection be with him on his way - and this is (Psalms 85:14), "righteousness [tzedek] shall go before him," meaning the attribute of Tzedek.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:40: And so in his deeds, such as in washing his hands, to give dominance to the right over the left, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Miketz, page 198b), and likewise every time, he should not give dominance to the left foot over the right, nor the left hand over the right hand, but rather the opposite: the right hand over the left, the right foot over the left, always, and with the intent to subdue the external force.
